channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD steadies around $69.00 amid US bond buybacks
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) remains stronger for the fourth successive day, trading around $69.00 per troy ounce during the European hours on Monday. Silver price rises as concerns over United States (US) debt management and fiscal sustainability persist.

item.title: Forex Today: Majors stay quiet as investors await US' 'economic D-Day' sanctions
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Monday, August 24:

item.title: US Dollar: Momentum fades as yields stay high – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes that the Dollar has extended its recent soft patch even as US Q3 GDP forecasts are upgraded to 2.5% annualized from 2.0%. Elevated fiscal deficits and long-end Treasury yields are weighing on sentiment.

item.title: Gold eases from mid-May highs as bulls await details of Iran sanctions
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) retreats slightly from its highest level since mid-May, touched earlier this Monday, though it retains a positive bias and trades around $4,630 during the first half of the European session.

item.title: Euro: ECB patience with inflation and growth tension – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY notes that Europe is seeking a Goldilocks mix of improving activity without reigniting inflation, with Euro strength already tightening conditions.

item.title: British Pound holds near six-month highs as debt woes keep US Dollar rallies shallow
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) holds mild gains for the fourth consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) on a calm Monday session, as ongoing concerns about the US Treasury’s bond buyback plans keep US Dollar bulls subdued.

item.title: British Pound: Range-trade now, 1.3700 in sight against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note GBP/USD remains in a short-term consolidation, with price action confined between 1.3620 and 1.3665 after an overbought push to 1.3675.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade conflict weighs on Loonie – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister says the latest breakdown in US–Canada trade talks and Ottawa’s planned retaliatory tariffs point to a potentially protracted trade conflict.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds near June highs, above 0.7150 ahead of expected Iran sanctions
item.description: The AUD/USD pair extends the sideways consolidative price move near its highest level since early June, touched on Friday, and holds steady above mid-0.7100s through the early European session.

item.title: ECB's Cipollone: Risk of economic stagnation and sharp inflation rise is rather remote
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said that ‌the risk of economic stagnation and a sharp increase in inflation due to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz is rather remote, Reuters reported on Monday.

item.title: Indian Rupee moves little amid RBI support, lower oil
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) maintains its position against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, positioning itself for a quiet start to the week.

item.title: Canadian Dollar declines as US-Canada trade talks collapse
item.description: The USD/CAD pair recovers some lost ground to near 1.3820 during the early European session on Monday. The Canadian Dollar (CAD) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) after US-Canada talks collapse into a trade war.

item.title: Gold: Upside risks building as fiscal worries grow – ING
item.description: ING Commodities Strategist Ewa Manthey highlights that Gold has rebounded from its July lows near $4,000/oz to around $4,600/oz, supported by renewed investment demand, a weaker Dollar and mounting concerns over the US fiscal outlook.

item.title: WTI Oil flirts with the $85.00 level as markets await economic D-Day sanctions on Iran
item.description: Crude prices are trimming some of last week’s gains on Monday. The US benchmark West Texas Intermediate Oil is changing hands at $85.35, with investors awaiting details of a new package of US sanctions against Iran that might extend to Russia or China.

item.title: Equities: Resilience supported by strong macro – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team reports that Equities ended Friday higher, though several markets, especially in the US, finished the week lower. The team stresses that robust macro and earnings data, plus sector leadership from Materials over Utilities, show no defensive rotation.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Psychological resistance and intervention fears – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Teppei Ino reviews recent USD/JPY trading ahead of Jackson Hole. The pair opened near 159 and repeatedly tested the 160 level, which acted as psychological resistance as traders watched for possible Japanese intervention.

item.title: Euro: Upside room toward 1.1800 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann keep a constructive view on EUR/USD after the pair held near 1.1680 and tested 1.1710 twice.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Holds steady below 1.1700 as overbought momentum tempers further gains
item.description: The EUR/USD pair holds steady near 1.1680 during the early European trading hours on Monday. Fiscal interventions from the US Treasury weigh on the US Dollar (USD) against the Euro (EUR). Traders brace for details of sanctions on Iran and a policy ‌speech this week in the United States (US).

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah declines despite prevailing high interest rates, weaker US Dollar
item.description: USD/IDR gains ground after three days of losses, trading around 17,740 during the Asian hours on Monday. However, the currency pair could face headwind pressure as the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) may draw renewed support from lingering high interest rates.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Consolidates near June high as bulls await breakout through 0.6000
item.description: The NZD/USD pair enters a bullish consolidation phase at the start of a new week and trades around the 0.5975 region during the Asian session, just below its highest level since June, touched on Friday.

item.title: Swiss Franc advances as Dollar slides on US bond buyback surge
item.description: USD/CHF depreciates after two days of gains, trading around 0.8000 during the Asian hours on Monday. The currency pair depreciates as the US Dollar (USD) struggles under pressure from newly announced fiscal measures in Washington.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Softens to near 185.50, but maintaining constructive bias above 100-day SMA
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross trades with mild losses near 185.60 during the early European session on Monday.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds bullish below $70.00/two-month high set on Friday
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) seesaws between tepid gains and minor losses around the $69.00 mark through the Asian session on Monday. The white metal, however, remains within striking distance of a two-month high, around the $70.00 psychological mark touched on Friday, and seems poised to appreciate further.

item.title: United States Dollar Index softens below 99.00 on US fiscal concerns
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), an index of the value of the US Dollar (USD) measured against a basket of six world currencies, currently trades near 98.80 in the Asian trading hours on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen advances on BoJ rate hike bets, subdued US Dollar
item.description: USD/JPY extended its losses for the second straight day after intraday volatility, trading around 158.80 during Asian hours on Monday. The pair declines as the Japanese Yen (JPY) gains ground on stronger-than-expected inflation data, which accelerated for a second straight month.

item.title: Canadian Dollar bears seem hesitant as weak USD counters US-Canada trade war
item.description: The USD/CAD pair struggles to capitalize on a bullish gap opening on Monday, though it retains an intraday positive bias amid concerns about a deepening US-Canada trade war.

item.title: Gold gains momentum above $4,600 on US Treasury buyback plans
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) gains traction to around $4,625 during the early Asian trading hours on Monday. The precious metal climbs to the highest since May 15 as the US Treasury's buyback support plan weighs on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: WTI slips below $85.00 as traders take profits before new US sanctions on Iran
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price depreciates after two days of gains, trading around $84.80 per barrel during the Asian hours on Monday. Crude oil prices decline as investors took profits ahead of an expected US announcement regarding stricter sanctions against Iran.

item.title: British Pound holds near Feb. 11 highs vs weak USD as bulls await breakout above 1.3660
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades with a positive bias around mid-1.3600s at the start of a new week and remains well within striking distance of its highest level since February 11, touched on Friday.
